title: Ganesh Chaturthi
description: A 10-day grand festival honoring the birth of Lord Ganesha.
rituals: Clay Ganesha idol installation in homes and public pandals
Ganesh Visarjan (submerging idol in water body)
significance: Celebrates the arrival of Ganesha to Earth from Kailash, bringing wisdom, prosperity, and obstacle removal.

title: Maha Shivratri
description: The great night of Lord Shiva celebrated annually in reverence.
rituals: Bathing the Shiva Lingam with water, milk, honey, and Bilva leaves
significance: Signifies the night Lord Shiva performed the cosmic dance of creation and destruction, and married Goddess Parvati.

title: Durga Puja & Navratri
description: The nine-night festival celebrating Goddess Durga's victory over Mahishasura.
rituals: Fasting during the nine days and worshipping the nine avatars of Durga
Reciting Durga Saptashati and Durga Chalisa
significance: Celebrates the triumph of divine energy and good over evil.

title: Ram Navami
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
rituals: Visiting Rama temples and offering fruits and flowers
significance: Marks the birth of Lord Rama and inspires devotees to follow the path of truth, righteousness, and devotion.

title: Hanuman Jayanti
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Hanuman, the symbol of strength, devotion, and courage.
rituals: Offering sindoor, jasmine oil, and laddus
Performing Hanuman Aarti and visiting Hanuman temples
significance: Honors Lord Hanuman's unwavering devotion to Lord Rama and seeks blessings for strength, protection, and wisdom.

title: Janmashtami
description: Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
rituals: Observing a day-long fast until midnight
Singing Krishna Bhajans and performing Jhulan celebrations
Organizing Dahi Handi events and Krishna Leelas
significance: Marks the birth of Lord Krishna and celebrates his teachings of love, devotion, and righteousness.

title: Govardhan Puja
description: Commemorates Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill to protect the people of Vrindavan.
rituals: Preparing Annakut with a variety of food offerings
significance: Celebrates faith in God, gratitude for nature, and the protection provided by Lord Krishna.

title: Vaikuntha Ekadashi
description: One of the most sacred Ekadashi observances dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
rituals: Visiting Vishnu temples and passing through the Vaikuntha Dwaram
significance: It is believed that observing this Ekadashi grants spiritual merit and the blessings of Lord Vishnu.

title: Narasimha Jayanti
description: Celebrates the appearance of Lord Narasimha, the fourth incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
rituals: Offering flowers and sweets to Lord Narasimha
significance: Commemorates the victory of righteousness over evil and Lord Vishnu's protection of Prahlada.

title: Chhath Puja
description: Ancient Vedic festival dedicated to Lord Surya and Chhathi Maiya.
rituals: Offering Arghya to the setting and rising Sun
significance: Expresses gratitude to Lord Surya for sustaining life and seeks health, prosperity, and family well-being.

title: Ratha Saptami
description: Celebrates the symbolic birth and glory of Lord Surya.
rituals: Taking a holy bath before sunrise
Reciting Aditya Hridayam and Surya Ashtakam
significance: Dedicated to Lord Surya for good health, vitality, and prosperity.

title: Vasant Panchami
description: Festival dedicated to Goddess Saraswati, the deity of wisdom, learning, music, and arts.
significance: Celebrates knowledge, wisdom, creativity, and the arrival of spring.

title: Saraswati Puja
description: A special worship of Goddess Saraswati, especially observed in schools and educational institutions.
rituals: Offering books, pens, and musical instruments to the Goddess
significance: Invokes the blessings of Goddess Saraswati for wisdom, education, and artistic excellence.
